parts.title: A GLASS Trolley? Why Supermarket Trolleys Are Made of METAL (Part 1) | Choosing Materials
parts.description:
A supermarket trolley: glass, metal or fabric? First find out what a trolley is FOR, then look closer: a loaded metal trolley, a hard knock, and a glass fish tank next door. Be the metal! Part 1 of Primary 3 Science, Diversity of materials: choosing materials.

In this part:
• What is a trolley for? Its purpose
• Look closer: the loaded metal trolley (the bars stay straight; a hard knock, no crack)
• Glass is fragile, fabric is flexible: why not a glass or fabric trolley?
• HOLD ON! Is glass a bad material?
• Look closer: a glass fish tank (transparent and waterproof)
• Be the metal: a bar at the bottom of the trolley
• Spot the hidden mynah!

Key words: purpose, physical properties.
Watch Part 2: three water bottles and one car with four materials! Last episode: see-through, blurry or blocked? Light and materials.

TheOneApp, Explained: Singapore primary science, made fun. Play along with Pip, Basil and Momo: show fingers to lock in, keep score on your hand, beat the Buddies!

Singapore Primary 3 Science (2023 syllabus): Diversity of materials (Chapter 3, pp. 59-65). Why isn't a trolley made of glass? Choosing materials. P3 Science, Chapter 3, Diversity of Materials: objects and their purposes, how physical properties decide what a material is used for, and why one object can use many materials. Also fits US NGSS 2-PS1-2 (Grade 2 and 3).
Safety: in this video an adult pushes the trolley, holds the bottles and pours the water. We never drop glass. Trolleys are for groceries, not for rides. In a car park, always stay with an adult.
Try it at home: pick one object at home. Tell someone at home what it is for, what it is made of, and which property makes that material suitable.
Singapore and the US: at a neighbourhood supermarket in Singapore we push a trolley; in the US (Grade 2 and 3) it is a shopping cart, and a windscreen is a windshield. The science is the same: the properties of a material decide what it is used for.

parts.title: One Car, FOUR Materials! Why Not Just One? (Part 2) | Choosing Materials
parts.description:
Plastic, glass or metal: which water bottle goes to school? Then look closer at one car, part by part: rubber tyres, fabric seats, a glass windscreen, a metal body. Be a drop of water! Part 2 of Primary 3 Science, Diversity of materials: choosing materials.

In this part:
• Look closer: three bottles, one object, three materials
• One object, different materials: the choice depends on the use
• Look closer: one car, four materials
• Be a drop of water: glass, metal, rubber
• Showdown: find the mistake in Momo's notes
• A chant to remember it all
• Spot the hidden squirrel!

Key words: use, parts, suitable.
Watch Part 1 first! Next episode: design a school bag like an engineer.
